report: Reviewed the complete qualified_names claim, its sole ordinary validate.rs implementation entry, and both complete ordinary test bodies. Independently verified exact byte equality of validate.rs, language.rs and value_types.rs with the historical reviewed source snapshots; the prior rationale remains supported by current evidence, rather than accepted solely from its verdict. Model construction records each declaration under its owning namespace and manifest dependencies. resolve_type delegates crate/$ paths to resolve_path, rejects unrooted segmented paths and self, and otherwise checks parameters, the current namespace and the prelude only; no sibling/root search occurs. resolve_path resolves crate against the owning crate and rejects external crates lacking a declared dependency (same-crate $ spelling is not cross-crate). Recursive tuple/argument resolution and value/class field/result callers retain these restrictions. The module_lookup_requires_qualification_for_root_and_sibling_types test asserts successful crate::Root and crate::one::Sibling references, then exactly one appropriate diagnostic for Root, Sibling and one::Sibling. generic_types_resolve_across_crates_with_dependency_checks asserts successful $lib::Wrapper<Vec<bool>> with depends $lib and an undeclared-dependency diagnostic without it. Thus explicit root/sibling qualification, forbidden implicit searches and declared cross-crate dependencies have direct positive/negative assertions; removing namespace restrictions or dependency enforcement would fail them. Captured the language.rs import context; other relied-on helpers are within the initial complete validate.rs fragment. No TODO/N/A entries or deferred prerequisites exist. This is source-inspection and baseline-comparison evidence. I executed review start/read and comparison commands, and am recording this report; I did not execute behavioral tests or cargo build. The coordinator separately reports 321 functional tests and a successful build; those are not my executions. No source changes or requested edits.
